messages:
morgan: proposal — add a small authn-authority service that canonicalizes incoming API keys and emits a deterministic origin_claim for routing/quotas/telemetry. this would simplify fallback logic when project bindings are missing and make dashboards more reliable. thoughts?

anika: how is this different from the existing auth proxy? seems like duplicate functionality.

morgan: auth proxy mixes responsibilities (authn, authz, billing attribution, sampling). authn-authority would be single-purpose: resolve key -> canonical origin, produce signed origin_claim header, and return a compact attribution map for quota systems.

sam: extra hop worries me. can we avoid p99 regressions for hosted API?

morgan: we only call it on first request per connection or when token changes. cache origin_claim per key at the edge (10m TTL). subsequent requests bypass the service. that keeps steady-state cost negligible.

jules: telemetry benefit is big: current logs have fuzzy attribution when keys are rotated or unbound. a canonical claim like org:123:proj:456:key:hash will unify joins across telemetry, billing, and dashboards.

dave: need to clarify impersonation semantics. service accounts can impersonate projects — precedence must be explicit.

morgan: precedence sketch: 1) explicit project claim encoded in token -> authoritative 2) impersonation/delegation header validated -> next 3) key metadata binding -> origin_claim 4) none -> label as "unattributed" and route to sandbox quota with sampled traces.

anika: for console UX, ops want to see unattributed spikes + quick action to rebind keys. can we include sample traces and validation-failure reason in the UI?

morgan: yes. plan is a tablified view: origin_claim | attributed_tokens | unattributed_tokens | last_seen | sample_trace_link. clicking trace opens the trace with the validation error highlighted.

sam: how will this affect historical billing/metrics? if attribution rules change during rollout we could get inconsistent aggregates.

jules: include origin_schema label (v1/v2) on telemetry so we can backfill and run attribution-diff joins. also emit snapshot_id for mappings.

dave: rollout idea: feature-flagged rollout at 10% traffic canary, run daily attribution-diff job, trigger alert if billed token delta > 1% or unattributed_rate increases.

morgan: agreed. key canary metrics: attribution_match_rate, unattributed_rate, extra_latency_p50/p99. infra-bot: checklist below.

infra-bot: Deploy checklist:
- create feature flag `authn_authority` (default off)
- provision edge cache (redis) with per-key TTL (10m default)
- add telemetry labels: origin_claim, origin_schema, origin_snapshot_id
- dashboards: attribution_match_rate, unattributed_tokens, attributed_tokens_by_org
- quota pipeline: honor X-Origin-Claim header when present; preserve old behaviour as fallback
- security: sign origin_claim with control-plane KMS; attach X-Origin-Sig header

anika: security ask noted — downstream services must verify signature; otherwise we allow spoofing.

morgan: origin_claim will be signed (HMAC via KMS) and services will validate X-Origin-Sig. key rotation for signing keys will be recorded in origin_snapshot_id.

sam: i'll take a perf prototyping slot this week. can you open a tiny PR with sequence diagram and prototype flag?

morgan: i'll open PR with README, sequence diagram, sample headers and validation pseudo-code. sample headers:
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Origin-Claim: org:123:proj:456:key:ab12cd
X-Origin-Sig: v1:hmacsha256=...

jules: finance wants a query to compute attribution deltas so they can reconcile invoices during migration. please add.

dave: also add a customer-facing migration note in console for teams depending on per-key billing attribution.

morgan: will do. tagging @sam for perf review and @anika for console UX. i'll post PR and canary playbook when ready. :eyes:
